cross_cutting.title: The D11/D12 FIGURE_REGISTRY registration is inert - the round-2 root cause is NOT closed
cross_cutting.detail: Seven FigureSpec entries were added at scripts/review_figures.py:1862-1985, but neither func_map dict was extended: generate_figures()'s map at line 2164 and run_structural_checks()'s map at line 2530 both lack every fig_d11_*/fig_d12_* key, and the lookup is a plain func_map.get(spec.function) with no getattr or importlib fallback. Executing generate_figures() with FIGURE_REGISTRY narrowed to the four D11 specs prints 'SKIP <name>: function <fn> not found' four times, returns {}, and writes zero files. figures/review_manifest.json and figures/structural_checks.json therefore still contain zero occurrences of 'd11' and are still dated 2026-06-14. Beyond the wiring: FigureSpec has no output_dir field and generate_figures() hardcodes FIGURES_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT/'figures' with write_image(..., width=1200, height=800, scale=2), so even after wiring the D11 PNGs would land in figures/ rather than papers/D11/figures/ where the .tex consumes them, AND would be re-rendered at 1200x800 - overriding each function's own canvas (900x580, 1120x580, 1080x600) and reflowing every annotation position, silently forking the reviewed image from the shipped image. Neither of the two checks round 2 asked for exists.
cross_cutting.fix: (1) Import the seven functions and add them to BOTH func_map dicts (lines ~2164 and ~2530). (2) Add 'output_dir: str | None = None' to FigureSpec; in generate_figures() resolve out_dir = PROJECT_ROOT / spec.output_dir if spec.output_dir else FIGURES_DIR, and omit the width/height kwargs from write_image so the figure's own layout size is honoured; set output_dir='papers/D11/figures' on the four D11 specs and the D12 equivalent. (3) Add check_shape_layers(): for every entry of fig.layout.shapes, raise an error when shape.layer != 'below' while the corresponding subplot carries traces. (4) Add check_no_inimage_ordinal(): regex the rendered title/annotation text for r'Fig\.?\s*\d+' and error on any hit, so figure numbering can only ever live in LaTeX.

cross_cutting.detail: paper_draft.tex is revtex4-2 [aps,prb,reprint], measured \columnwidth = 246.0 pt and \textwidth = 510.0 pt. All four figures are single-column figure environments with \includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]. None of the four functions sets font=, so all four inherit plotly's 12 px default rather than the project's canonical FONT (visualizations.py:69-75, size 14). summary: Round 3 confirms that both round-2 FAILs are genuinely and completely fixed at the level they were reported. XC-A is verified independently at the pixel level: an exhaustive sweep for every plausible composite of carmine, steel blue and amber under the amber-0.20, blue-0.12, blue-0.14 and blue-0.20 overlays returns zero exact matches across all four PNGs, connected-component analysis gives three exact-carmine clusters of exactly 612 px in Fig 3 (reproducing the claim to the pixel), Fig 4's in-plot markers and legend swatch are all exact carmine so the marker does match its own legend swatch, and Fig 3's K' curve reads exactly (241,143,1) both inside and outside the shaded window. XC-B is verified in the compiled PDF: the in-image ordinals are gone and paper_draft.aux/the rendered pages agree on FIG. 1 phononic, FIG. 2 PT, FIG. 3 effective-medium, FIG. 4 Haldane. Remediations 3, 4 and 6 landed cleanly. The physics was recomputed from scratch and is exact on every anchor, and the highest-priority anchor PASSES with zero hits: no figure contains any Berry-curvature, continuum-Chern-integral or bulk-boundary string, and the draft prose explicitly disclaims all three. The bundle nevertheless does NOT meet the ALL-PASS criterion, for two FAIL-class reasons.
